subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: p and q are the lengths of the perpendiculars from the origin to the straight lines x sec α + y cosec α = a and x cos α − y sin α = a cos 2α. Prove that 4p² + q² = a².

mark_split.label: Set up p from the origin

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.155, chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 9. **Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work** — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split follows the shape of the proof: two marks each on the two genuine pieces of work, simplifying sec²α + cosec²α and reading off q, two more on adding the two results, and one each on setting up p and turning it into 4p². This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C prints 3 long answer questions at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The identity was checked numerically before it was written: at a = 5 and α = 30° the two perpendicular lengths are p = 5√3/4 ≈ 2.1651 and q = 2.5, giving 4p² + q² = 18.75 + 6.25 = 25 = a². The step for p was also checked a second way, by multiplying the first line through by sin α cos α, which turns it into x sin α + y cos α = a sin α cos α and gives the same p in one line.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name the distance formula you use for each line, and say what identity closes the proof.

steps.label: Set up p from the origin
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the line with 0 on the right, then put x = 0 and y = 0 into |ax + by + c|/√(a² + b²). Keep the modulus bars: p is a length.
lines: Here sin α ≠ 0 and cos α ≠ 0, so that
sec α and cosec α are defined.
First line:  x sec α + y cosec α − a = 0

recall.must_convey: That p is |a| divided by √(sec²α + cosec²α), from the distance formula with the origin put in.
accept: p is mod a over root sec squared plus cosec squared
put x equals zero and y equals zero in the distance formula
the perpendicular from the origin leaves only the constant on top
origin nunchi distance formula lo zero zero pettali
p equals mod of a by root of sec square plus cosec square

steps.why: The perpendicular length from the origin is the distance formula with x = 0 and y = 0 put in, and a length is never negative, so the modulus bars are written from the first line.
common_mistakes: Dropping the modulus bars and writing p = −a/√(sec²α + cosec²α).
Using the coefficients of the line before it is written with 0 on the right side.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular from the ORIGIN means put x = 0 and y = 0 into the distance formula, so only the constant term is left on the top.

steps.label: Simplify sec²α + cosec²α
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Change both terms to sines and cosines, add over the common denominator sin²α cos²α, and use sin²α + cos²α = 1 on the top.

recall.must_convey: That sec²α + cosec²α = 1/(sin²α cos²α), so p = |a sin α cos α|.
accept: sec squared plus cosec squared is one over sin squared cos squared
add them over the common denominator and the top becomes one
so p is mod a sin alpha cos alpha
common denominator theesukunte one by sin square cos square vasthundi
the root gives one over mod sin alpha cos alpha
heard_as: one over sin squared cos squared

steps.why: Turning the two squared reciprocals into one fraction is what makes the square root come out exactly, and that is the only real difficulty in the whole proof.
common_mistakes: Writing sec²α + cosec²α = 1/(sin²α + cos²α), adding the denominators.
Taking √(1/(sin²α cos²α)) as 1/(sin α cos α), losing the modulus bars.
steps.memory_tip: sec² + cosec² adds to ONE over sin² cos². The top collapses to 1 because sin²α + cos²α = 1.

steps.label: Write 4p² using sin 2α
steps.margin_note: One mark. Double p first, so the double angle appears, and only then square. Squaring removes the modulus by itself.
lines: Now 2 sin α cos α = sin 2α, so

recall.must_convey: That doubling gives 2p = |a sin 2α|, so 4p² = a² sin²2α.
accept: two sin alpha cos alpha is sin two alpha
double p first so four p squared is a squared sin squared two alpha
the double angle turns p into sin two alpha
double angle formula vaadithe sin two alpha vasthundi
four p squared equals a squared sin squared two alpha

steps.why: The second line carries cos 2α, so the first one has to be pushed into a double angle as well before the two can be added.
common_mistakes: Writing 2p = a sin 2α and then 4p² = 2a² sin²2α.
Forgetting to double p before squaring, and writing p² = a² sin²2α.
steps.memory_tip: Double FIRST, square second. 2 sin α cos α is sin 2α, so 2p carries sin 2α and 4p² carries sin²2α.

steps.label: Find q
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The coefficients here are cos α and −sin α, so the square root at the bottom is exactly 1. Keep the modulus bars until you square.
lines: Second line:  x cos α − y sin α − a cos 2α = 0

recall.must_convey: That q = |a cos 2α| because cos²α + sin²α = 1.
accept: the bottom is root cos squared plus sin squared which is one
q is mod a cos two alpha
q squared is a squared cos squared two alpha
denominator one avuthundi so q equals mod a cos two alpha
the second line already has cos and sin as coefficients

steps.why: The second line is already written with cos α and sin α as its coefficients, so its square root is 1 and q comes out in one move.
common_mistakes: Writing √(cos²α + sin²α) as cos α + sin α.
Dropping the cos 2α and writing q = |a|.
steps.memory_tip: The second line is ALREADY in normal shape: cos²α + sin²α = 1, so the bottom is 1 and q is just the constant term.

steps.label: Add and finish
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Add the two numbered results (1) and (2), take a² out, and use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 at θ = 2α.

recall.must_convey: That adding (1) and (2) and using sin²2α + cos²2α = 1 gives a².
accept: add the two results and sin squared plus cos squared is one
take a squared out and the bracket becomes one
four p squared plus q squared equals a squared
rendu kalipithe a square vasthundi
the identity at two alpha finishes the proof

steps.why: Both results were pushed to the same angle 2α on purpose, so that sin²2α + cos²2α = 1 closes the proof in one line.
common_mistakes: Adding sin²2α + cos²2α and writing 2 instead of 1.
Leaving the answer as a²(sin²2α + cos²2α) without finishing.
steps.memory_tip: Both pieces were written at the SAME angle 2α on purpose. Add them and sin² + cos² = 1 does the rest.
